I am a physician, board certified in internal medicine, living in a state with a 6 week abortion ban.  
Here are my comments on proposed rule VA-2025-VHA-0073-0002.
1. Under the proposed rule, as under EMTALA, any Veteran in the US who has a life threatening complication of pregnancy should
be able to get emergency care, including abortion if there is no other option. My Ob-GYN colleagues specialized in Maternal-Fetal Medicine point out that
this care, whether life-saving for both mother and fetus or for mother only,  is technically difficult. With this regulation in place, who will be left within the VA system with the training and experience to give this care?
2. The proposed rule makes no exception for rape, incest, fatal fetal abnormality, or fetal conditions that are catastrophic to families, but not immediately fatal.  Some, like congenital Zika, are more likely in mothers who have been deployed overseas.  This means that, contrary to promises made to our service members, families receiving care under the VA system have substantially less healthcare benefits than most Americans!  It is shocking.  Congress must devise a workaround for them.
3. There are many medical conditions which are exacerbated by pregnancy.  The mother may not die but she may have a disabling complication.  These include lupus, epilepsy and severe migraine. 
Other medical conditions are best treated with medications that can cause fetal abnormalities, aka birth defects.  These include cancer chemotherapy agents, major psychiatric disorders and rheumatoid arthritis.  Veterans receiving these medications are advised to use birth control, but no birth control method is 100% safe.  Good specialty care for these veterans must include counseling about the risks of remaining pregnant.  Again, give our veterans the standard of care that applies to the civilian population.
Thank you for your consideration.
